Apparently, I am not the only one impatient for Matty ( Kathy Bates ) and Olympia ( Skye P. Marshall ) to make up already on Matlock. Matty is also pushing for the pair to make up sooner rather than later , but Olympia is still taking time to process everything that has happened between the two of them. However, the job still requires them to work closely with each other, and the cracks in Olympia’s emotional walls are getting bigger and bigger with each and every case. There’s still hope, and we’ll have to cling to it for as long as we can. Matty and Olympia aren’t the only ones trying to forge new bonds in the office. Senior ( Beau Bridges ) sends Sarah ( Leah Lewis ) on a mission to get pictures of Julian’s ( Jason Ritter ) date book because Senior believes Julian is going to “poach clients” when he leaves. It’s more likely that Senior is suspicious of Eva’s ( Justina Machado ) constant presence in the New York office, but the snooping mission leads Sarah to genuinely bond with Julian. They both are kooky weirdos, and Julian grows to really appreciate Sarah, once he gets over the clinginess. Is he going to be able to deal when he finds out she was on his case on a mission for his father, though? Someone stop kicking this man while he’s down! Senior may be just starting to dig into Eva’s presence in the office, but we already know what’s going down. Matty and Olympia are helping her with a coup , which means some high-stakes action is coming to the Jacobson Moore office very soon. The Cruel Face of Addiction Appears in 'Matlock' Season 2, Episode 6 Marlene Forte as Sister Louise and Kathy Bates as Matty on Matlock via CBS Eva’s surface-level plans for her return trip to New York involve helping some nun friends with a zoning board hearing so they can continue running a homeless shelter out of their convent. She hands the case over to Olympia and team, who promptly handle the zoning board, only to find the nuns in the crosshairs of a civil suit when a rogue 9-1-1 call leads to drugs being found on the church premises. They’ve been allowing addicts to do “reduction of harm” shoot ups to help them survive the night, but that causes a visceral backlash against the convent when a video of a woman overdosing outside the church is shown in court. It’s a lot for the judge and the jury to see, and it’s also a lot for Matty to handle. Finding out that the nuns are giving addicts drugs hits a very sensitive nerve for Matty, who is immediately reminded of her daughter Ellie. It is always sad having to watch Matty confront the grief of losing her daughter, but this struggle isn’t just to give Kathy Bates more material for her Emmy reel. Working with the nuns helps Matty reacquaint herself with the human side of addiction — addicts are people that are trying. It makes her more lenient when it comes to Olympia not jumping to forgive her and it also makes her more understanding that Alfie’s father Joey can’t be “perfect in his sobriety.” The empathy we were hoping to see in Matty returns . Giving Joey some lenience when it comes to writing Alfie every day helps Alfie relax that his birth father doesn’t have to be a saint for him to have hope of having a relationship with him. Matty’s ability to find forgiveness in the face of such a triggering case also helps Olympia find her way a little closer to reconciling their friendship. She also expects Matty to be perfect, but that isn’t realistic. There’s going to be some back and forth and they have to figure out some way to be okay with that. In the end, the nuns lose the ability to provide controlled doses of narcotics to addicts, but retain the right to run a homeless shelter. They’re going to continue fighting the good fight, while Matty and Olympia turn their attention to their own massive battle. Posts By Giovana Gelhoren Sep 29, 2025 The Coup Is A-Go When Olympia Brings in a New Ally Kathy Bates as Matty and Phil Buckman as Father Patrick Cassidy on Matlock via CBS Eva is ready to make her move on Senior at the next quarterly meeting, but she needs Olympia (and Matty’s) help to recruit votes from partners in the New York office to actually oust the managing partner. That means that Olympia and Matty have to surreptitiously ask around to find people in their corner without Senior finding out that a vote is being gathered. Matty manages to scrounge up the votes, but then Eva loses a partner from the Miami office, which leaves them one short again. Welcome, Father Patrick Cassidy ( Phil Buckman ), to the fold. He was a former partner at the firm and then left to join the church. He initially comes in to help Olympia with the nun’s case, but it’s clear from the jump that there is no love lost between him and Senior. He even refers to him as the devil. So when Matty approaches him about the vote, he’s all in. As an emeritus partner, he retains voting rights, and he would love to be the nail Senior’s professional coffin. That seems…easy. Too easy! Matty, Olympia, and Eva are ready to move forward with the plan, but Senior has been one step ahead throughout the entire series . Is he really clueless about what Eva is planning or that Olympia is helping him? It doesn’t seem so, especially with Senior going to Sarah for help. Sarah’s Side Mission Could Destroy Everything Leah Lewis as Sarah on Matlock via CBS Sarah is as shocked as anyone to find Senior approaching her while she prepares for the nun trial. A chance run-in with her parents in an earlier episode tells Senior that Sarah is ambitious, and he’s ready to use her to get dirt on Julian. He wants photos of Julian’s date book from the past six months and claims it is to make sure it is so Julian won’t poach any clients when he eventually finds a new job. It takes Sarah a couple of weeks to worm her way into Julian’s good graces, but when she gets there, it is clear the two share a real bond . She helps him secure a meeting with a technology solutions firm — his first client signing since losing partner and being demoted. It puts a real pep back in Julian’s step, and it’s obvious he and Sarah have a rapport unlike any other relationship in the office. He even promises that he’ll hand over the client to her when he leaves the firm because he knows there’s a no-poaching rule. Sarah naively thinks this confession will be enough to assuage Senior, and she won’t actually have to betray Julian’s trust. Sorry, poor girl, you are having a terrible first time at the rodeo. Senior wants what he wants, so Sarah returns and gets the photos. This is the first time we’ve seen Julian in a good mood since he lost the partner race to Olympia. He was starting to see the light at the end of his own tunnel, but if he finds out that this unexpected good luck is tainted by his father’s manipulations, it is going to crush him . It’s also terrible for Sarah, who has a very hard time making solid connections in the office, to have to betray someone who could actually be her mentor. Once again, Senior is ruining everything. Let’s hope that she and Julian can find a way out of this unscathed. But can we please not have that and Senior finding out about the partner vote happen at the same time? That might be too much to wish for in this imperfect world. Matlock continues Thursdays at 9PM ET on CBS. The social media announcement lists the cast over a recording of “I’ll Be Seeing You” by Vera Lynn, which is set to include series favorites Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe, and Leslie Grossman. New to the franchise is Wicked: For Good star Ariana Grande , who previously teamed up with Murphy on the horror-comedy series Scream Queens . And, as the announcement teases with a lengthy pause, Jessica Lange is making her return to the series, after last being seen briefly in 2018\'s Apocalypse season. The two-time Oscar winner previously starred in five seasons of the show, beginning with the inaugural Murder House . Despite her status as a perennial fan favorite, Lange had previously intimated in the past that she had no plans to return to the AHS televerse. In fact, on a red carpet earlier this year, when asked by an Irish radio station if she would be in the 13th season, Lange said, "Oh Christ, no. I mean, I haven\'t done it for more than 10 years, 12 years, so, no, I\'m not doing it." When the reporter followed up to ask if she would do the new season if approached, she said simply, "No," before walking away. The theme for season 13 hasn\'t been unmasked, but prior seasons have tackled everything from a cult to a coven to aliens. Murphy usually teases out those reveals on his social media, so stay tuned for that. The AHS13 tease is a long time coming: When the next edition of American Horror Story releases, it will have been three years since the most recent season, Delicate , debuted. It’s another emotional day for Matty ( Kathy Bates ) and Olympia ( Skye P. Marshall ) on Matlock , as Olympia struggles through her father’s birthday, and their new case brings up painful memories of Ellie ( Marnee Carpenter ) for Matty. The duo are still working through their trust issues and being transparent, but that old spark is starting to show up again. They can’t take down Senior ( Beau Bridges ) if they aren’t on the same page, and that’s so much easier when they can admit they respect each other. However, by the end of the episode, Matty and Olivia’s tension is not their biggest problem. Julian ( Jason Ritter ) is using his job in compliance to help Olivia gain evidence on his dad, but he’s also on the hunt for the real mole at the firm. It’ll be a lot easier to find who actually reached out to Olympia and hand them over to Senior than to try and bring the titan down. So far, Julian has been in the dark about Matty’s Wellbrexa investigation, but is it time to give him the full picture? A Somber Trip Down Memory Lane in 'Matlock' Season 2, Episode 4 Christine Kellogg-Darrin as “Gloria Russo”, Leah Lewis as “Sarah Franklin” and Kathy Bates as “Madeline Matlock” in Matlock Season 2, Episode 4 Image via CBS Olympia and crew take on a wrongful death suit in the case of the week to help an elderly widow get the money she needs to survive after her husband dies while trapped in his factory during a hurricane. The key part of their case is playing the widow’s final voicemail from her husband, which will drive home the emotional devastation of the loss to the jury. It takes tricking their opposing counsel into making the audio admissible, but it is the ticket Olympia needs to get a reasonable settlement on the table for their client. Matty is already in her feelings during the case as she buddies up with Deborah Palmer ( Surprise, it’s Melanie Lynskey making her acting debut with Kathy Bates, dreams come true! ). Deborah is Senior’s paramour that he took to Australia during the Wellbrexa case, and now is a freelance makeup artist. Matty goes in for a makeover that is comically awful (think Tammy Faye-level bad) but they bond over karaoke because that’s what Deborah and Senior did together in Australia (thanks uncovered expense reports!). It’s also Ellie’s favorite pastime, and getting closer to Deborah has Matty remembering her daughter’s karaoke baby shower. Ellie was sober for the event, but only newly so. Past Matty couldn’t just trust her daughter and allow herself to have a good time. She went above and beyond to ensure that Ellie was staying sober for her kid, but her constant checking and need for assurances created a wider gulf between her and her daughter, and nearly ruined a perfectly good day. Ellie would actually relapse a few weeks later, but singing on stage with Deborah and listening to their client talk about not wasting time with her husband has Matty feeling very wistful throughout the episode. Posts By Rahul Malhotra Oct 15, 2025 It is always a bummer to see Matty rehash Ellie memories, especially hurtful ones. But the vulnerability allows her and Olympia to have their first real moment of connection in the second season . There are multiple moments in this episode where we see glimpses of their friendship, and they’re the best parts of the entire episode. Optimists hold in there. We are going to get these back to the good ol’ days eventually. It’s a reminder for Matty to live in the present and to be grateful for the life she has right now. The same can’t be said for Deborah, who definitely gets spooked by Matty continually asking who she was traveling with in Australia. When she evades Matty’s requests for a second karaoke date, Matty and Olympia surmise Senior had her sign an NDA. That means there’s a paper trail of damaging things being said in Australia, and they just have to find it . Luckily, they have a guy on the inside. Unluckily, that guy is also now suspicious of Matty’s involvement in the Wellbrexa investigation. Julian Is on the Trail, Is Time To Bring Him In? Senior’s latest attempt to humiliate Julian is to put him on the compliance committee, which means going around to every Jacobson Moore employee with the IT guy and briefing them on the new firm security measures after the leak. Olympia points out that this is a great opportunity for Julian to potentially get Senior’s login passwords so they can do the snooping they need to do to clear Julian of his wrongdoing in the Wellbrexa case. Julian comes up with a better idea when he spots Belvin’s ( Patricia Belcher ) login key and laptop by Senior’s assistant’s desk. He has his new IT buddy walk him through wiping the laptop clean and learns that Matty texted Belvin right before her meeting with the head of security. Senior’s old expense reports were also printed from Belvin’s account four minutes before that meeting, and Julian suspects that Matty is the one that printed them. She’s the one working with Belvin and therefore the real leaker . This seems like bad news on the surface. It gives Julian a lot of leverage in the whole investigation. It is a lot easier for him to hand Matty over to Senior and have him eviscerate her rather than continuing to risk his own neck to get the dirt on his dad. Matty absolutely won’t want him as part of the investigation. She’s having a hard enough time trusting Olympia. How could she possibly trust Julian when he hid the documents in the first place? However, as viewer, this is great. Jason Ritter is too good to have him play clueless for too long . Plus, one of Matty’s conditions for continuing to work with Olympia is that Julian has to apologize to her, Edwin ( Sam Anderson ), and Alfie ( Aaron Harris ). So she intends for him to find out it’s her eventually. Why not get the apology sooner rather than later, bring Julian into the investigation, and then we get Julian and Matty hijinks? The potential for both emotional depth and comedic gold is too great to ignore. Obviously, Olympia and Matty are going to try and throw him off the scent first, but having Julian in the know is a really exciting possibility as we head further into the sophomore season . The more people that know about the investigation, the higher the stakes. It’s so juicy! Will they figure out a way to rope him in, or is he doomed to be the investigation lap dog forever? It is one of the things that so many fans love about classics like Law & Order . They are digestible single-episode cases, and you can drop in at practically any point. That also means that there is rarely any development for the characters. However, Kathy Bates \' 2024 reboot of Matlock broke the traditional legal procedural formula, and does a brilliant job of balancing the case of the week with the larger storyline. What Is Kathy Bates\' CBS Series \'Matlock\' About? Matlock stars Jason Ritter, Kathy Bates, and Skye P. Marshall Image via: CBS Matlock is a gender-swapped reboot of Andy Griffith’s classic Matlock , which ran from 1986 to 1995. In the updated version, the series takes place in a world where the original series was also a fan-favorite legal drama and a favorite of protagonist Madeline Matlock’s daughter. Kathy Bates plays the titular role as a retired lawyer who moves her husband and grandson with her to New York, comes out of retirement, and joins the law firm that she suspects is responsible for the death of her daughter. Related CBS’ 95% RT Legal Drama Surges on Streaming as Viewers Flock for Season 2 Kathy Bates and Skye P. Marshall star in the twisty lawyer drama. Posts By Rahul Malhotra Oct 15, 2025 Besides Bates, the splendid cast also features Skye P. Marshal l as her co-lead, alongside others like Jason Ritter , Sam Anderson , and Leah Lewis . At the firm, Jacobson Moore, Bates, and Olympia (Marshall) work alongside first-year associates Sarah and Billy ( David Del Rio ). Jacobson Moore worked with WellBrexa, a pharmaceutical company, and Matty believes someone at the law firm hid documents that could\'ve prevented the opioid epidemic , which ultimately led to her daughter’s addiction and eventual overdose. \'Matlock\' Stands Out From Other Traditional Legal Procedurals in an Inventive Way If you look at Law & Order: Special Victims Unit , led by the fabulous Mariska Hargitay , each episode is a self-contained case. Largely, the cases don’t span multiple episodes, and the focus isn’t on overarching character arcs. This case-of-the-week legal procedural provides comfort food for fans who can drop in and watch any episode. Unfortunately, it also leads to characters tending to be static and not developing too much throughout the season. The focus is rarely on the regulars, which leads to storylines about their character growth moving at a snail\'s pace — or sometimes being nonexistent all together. For fans of serialized dramas, Matlock is a breath of fresh air. It’s one of the rare legal procedurals that seamlessly blends a case of the week with its overarching storyline led by Matlock and her search for truth . The case-of-the-week series tend to have limited coverage of a character, such as a romance or a personal story. Matlock allows for its characters to have multiple stories alongside the crime that week. For example, besides solving the case, Matlock is constantly balancing the true feelings and connections she is forming with Olympia, Sarah, and Billy with the reality that she\'s showing them a fake version of herself. This all comes to a tense moment when her husband expresses his worries about her stress levels, and an ambulance is even called. Instead of saving for one big reveal at the end of the season, Matlock follows in the footsteps of streaming shows, with cliffhangers and revelations occurring at the end of almost every episode. Better yet, the Matlock writers didn’t confine the storyline to just one season. In a recent Season 2 episode, Olympia revealed to Madeline that Julian suspects she is involved in the Welbrexa situation. The stakes seem higher, it doesn’t feel forced, and in Season 2, we get to see two influential lawyers pulling the strings and conspiring to uncover the truth . As more audiences expect serialized dramas and throughlines, this kind of story is perfect for the streaming era. Matty and Olympia\'s Dynamic Is Even More Complicated in \'Matlock\' Season 2 via CBS From the “sweet elderly lawyer” Matlock to the angry and hurt Madeline, to the complex grandma of Alfie, we get to see Bates\' brilliant character from all sides. In Season 2 , we also get to explore so many new stories. Olympia is now part of the Wellbrexa exposure plan , which creates an entirely new dynamic and plenty of opportunities for tension between the two leads. One moment in Season 2 that stands out is when Olympia and Matty have to show each other their phones because they don\'t trust one another. At the same time, Olympia covers for Matty with their colleagues and gives fake excuses for Matty\'s whereabouts. We get to see Olympia behave in a completely new way with Matty. She records an audio clip of Matty threatening her as leverage , which completely usurps the trust and friendship they built in the first season. Thanks to that relationship and that foundation, there is a part of Matty that wants to stay and help Olympia, and doesn’t want her family to get hurt as a result of their investigation. Bates has this kind of internal struggle masterfully on display. In addition, Olympia has to balance Matty while protecting the father of her children. Leaving this storyline in the first season would have been a huge missed opportunity. In a genre known for playing it safe, Matlock took a risk, and it\'s paying off in every possible way. Published Nov 15, 2025, 9:47 AM ET Updated Nov 15, 2025, 11:04 AM ET PUBLISHED Nov 15, 2025, 9:47 AM ET The US director Spike Lee gave Leo a basketball jersey at the meeting. Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/Reuters Facebook Tweet Email Link Link Copied! Hollywood stars met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican, where the pontiff called cinema a “workshop of hope” and lamented declining audiences. The line-up of film stars and directors meeting the first American pope on Saturday included Oscar-winners Cate Blanchett, known for “Aviator” and “Elizabeth”, and Spike Lee, who directed “Malcolm X” and “BlacKkKlansman”. All those present in the audience in the Vatican’s apostolic palace met Leo personally at the end, with Lee presenting the first American pope with a New York Knicks jersey. Monica Bellucci, who played Mary Magdalene in Mel Gibson’s “The Passion of the Christ”, also met the pope on Saturday, as did actor Adam Scott, of the series “Parks and Recreation” and “Severance”, and Sergio Castellitto, who played the “vaping cardinal” Tedesco in the movie “Conclave” that dramatizes the secretive papal election process. “The Church esteems you for your work with light and time, with faces and landscapes, with words and silence,” Leo told them. “I wish to renew this friendship because cinema is a workshop of hope, a place where people can once again find themselves and their purpose.” The meeting took place, the Vatican said, to “deepen dialogue with the World of Cinema” and explore the “possibilities that artistic creativity offers to the mission of the Church.” It also comes as the church is seeking to reach new audiences with a new Gallup World Poll showing a 17-point drop in the percentage of adults in the US who say religion is an important of their daily life. Pope Leo walks on the day of an audience with international filmmakers and actors, including Cate Blanchett, Spike Lee, Viggo Mortensen, Monica Bellucci, and Gus Van Sant. Simone Risoluti/Vatican Media/Reuters Cate Blanchett reacts in the Galleria Lapidaria of the Apostolic Palace after meeting Pope Leo. Matteo Minnella/Reuters In his speech, delivered in Italian, Leo also lamented the “troubling decline” of cinemas, which he said were increasingly being removed from cities. “I urge institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affirming the social and cultural value of this activity,” he said in remarks that were greeted by an applause. The Chicago-born pontiff had shared his favorite movies ahead of the meeting, naming “It’s a Wonderful Life” (1946), “The Sound of Music” (1965), “Ordinary People” (1980), and “Life is Beautiful” (1997). Rev. Antonio Spadaro, one of the Vatican officials helping to arrange the meeting, reflected that in each of Leo’s chosen films “goodness appears fragile, naïve, almost out of place – and yet precisely for that reason, revolutionary.” The Vatican meeting with film stars follows a similar gathering hosted by Pope Francis with comedians. The celebrity meeting was a sprinkling of star dust for a still relatively new pope and a way for the Catholic Church to engage more with the world beyond. It was also a strong show of support from Leo XIV for the global film industry, as he spoke out against the "troubling decline" in cinema-going. Hailed by director Spike Lee as a "great day", the gathering was the first of its kind in the Vatican. Beneath the magnificent frescoes of the Clementine Hall, Pope Leo spoke in Italian to praise the power of cinema to entertain and to educate â\x80\x93 and for its "capacity to amaze". But he urged filmmakers not to shy away from what he called "the world\'s wounds". "Violence, poverty, exile, loneliness, addiction and forgotten wars are issues that need to be acknowledged and narrated," the Pope said. "Good cinema does not exploit pain; it recognizes and explores it. This is what all the great directors have done." Six months since a conclave of cardinals elected the first North American to the Papacy, some Catholics feel that Leo has been slow to stamp his own mark on the role. His predecessor, Francis, was a charismatic Argentinian known for his off-the-cuff comments and dramatic gestures. Leo\'s style is far quieter, so this star-studded engagement is a new look. This week, the Vatican revealed that his favourite four watches of all time included the 1960s nun-themed classic The Sound of Music, It\'s a Wonderful Life and Italian Roberto Benigni\'s multi award-winning Life is Beautiful. Among those who did join today\'s A-list audience were Mortensen, Chris Pine and filmmaker Gus Van Sant â\x80\x93 of Milk and Good Will Hunting fame. The large Italian contingent included Gianni Amelio and Cinema Paradiso creator, Giuseppe Tornatore. At a time of immense pressure on film, not long after a major Hollywood strike and with funding strains here in Italy, the Pope spoke in defence of the industry. He was applauded loudly when he talked of the "quiet dedication" of all those behind the scenes with vital roles. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The audience for the international filmmakers was held beneath the magnificent frescoes of the Clementine Hall He also warned against the closure of cinemas which he characterised as the "beating heart of communities". "More than a few people are saying that the art of cinema and the cinematic experience are in danger. I urge institutions not to give up, but to cooperate in affirming the social and cultural value of this activity," the Pope said. After a fifteen-minute speech and a blessing he then received each audience member in turn, led by Blanchett . "He really urged us to go back into our day jobs and inspire people," the Australian-born star told reporters. One of many who came bearing gifts, the actress â\x80\x93 who works with the UN refugee agency, UNHCR â\x80\x93 placed a woven bracelet in the Pope\'s hand. "It was a bracelet I wear in solidarity with people who are displaced," she explained later. Lee handed the Chicago-born Pope a New York Knicks shirt printed with the number 14 and the words Pope Leo. There are no “Evil Dead” titles. “The Exorcist” is suspiciously absent. The list, in this case, is the favorite four films of Pope Leo XIV, f.k.a. Robert Francis Prevost of Chicago. The pontiff released the list via video ahead of a planned meeting Saturday with luminaries from the world of cinema. To avoid the risk of being played off the stage by the academy’s orchestra, let’s share the winners quickly: Advertisement 1. “It’s a Wonderful Life,” 1946 2. “The Sound of Music,” 1965 3. “Ordinary People,” 1980 4. “Life Is Beautiful,” 1997 That’s it. No “The Agony and the Ecstasy.” No “Pope Joan” or “Spotlight” or “Conclave,” for obvious reasons. No “Sister Act” or “Oh, God!” or any of the associated sequels, for less obvious reasons. For the record: 11:28 a.m. Nov. 14, 2025 A previous version of this story said the pope hadn’t chosen any films set near his hometown, Chicago. “Ordinary People” was set in a Chicago suburb. As a matter of fact, not a single comedy at all, much less a goofy comedy. And on either the drama or comedy fronts, the pope definitely could have chosen more than one flick set in his former neck of the woods. Think “The Blues Brothers,” “Home Alone,” “The Untouchables,” “High Fidelity,” “Eight Men Out” or “Ferris Bueller’s Day Off.” (Think “Chicago ,” for goodness’ sake.) Pope Leo will apparently be meeting Saturday with Hollywood types including, Variety reports, actors Monica Bellucci, Cate Blanchett, Alison Brie, Dave Franco, Viggo Mortensen and Chris Pine, plus directors Spike Lee, George Miller, Giuseppe Tornatore and Gus Van Sant. Seems the pope “has expressed his desire to deepen dialogue with the World of Cinema, and in particular with actors and directors, exploring the possibilities that artistic creativity offers to the mission of the Church and the promotion of human values,” according to a statement obtained by CNN . Advertisement That sounds all well and good, and a person can’t really go wrong with the movies on the pope’s list — two of the four are best picture Oscar winners, and the other two are best picture nominees. Leo, the first US pope, said cinema was a vital “workshop of hope” at a time of global uncertainty and digital overload. “Cinemas are experiencing a troubling decline, with many being removed from cities and neighborhoods,” he said. “More than a few people are saying that the art of cinema and the cinematic experience are in danger. A culture shaped by constant digital stimuli risks reducing stories to what algorithms predict will succeed, he said. “The logic of algorithms tends to repeat what works, but art opens up what is possible,” he said, urging filmmakers to defend “slowness, silence and difference” when they serve the story. The pope also encouraged artists to confront violence, war, poverty and loneliness with honesty, saying good cinema “does not exploit pain; it recognizes and explores it.” He praised not only directors and actors but the vast array of behind-the-scenes workers whose craft makes movies possible, calling filmmaking “a collective endeavor in which no one is self-sufficient.” At the end of his speech, the long list of invitees met the pope one-by-one, many offering him gifts, including Spike Lee, who gave him a New York Knicks basketball shirt emblazoned with “Pope Leo 14.” Ahead of Saturday’s meeting, the Vatican shared four of the pope’s favourite films: Robert Wise’s family musical The Sound of Music, Frank Capra’s feel-good It’s a Wonderful Life, Robert Redford’s heart-wrenching Ordinary People and Roberto Benigni’s sentimental World War Two drama Life Is Beautiful. – Rappler.com Summarize this article with AI Share in Chat Share article Facebook X (Twitter) Copy Link Copied How does this make you feel? The International Emmy Award-winning French dramedy series, which is set at a talent agency and features cameos from notable actors playing themselves, originally ran for four seasons from 2015 through 2020 and has a movie currently in development. Notable Call My Agent! guest stars have included Juliette Binoche, Christopher Lambert, Isabelle Huppert, Isabelle Adjani, Monica Bellucci, Sigourney Weaver, and Jean Reno. Per Variety , during a presentation at Taiwan Creative Content Fest, Organic Media Group revealed that they are developing a Chinese-language adaptation of Call My Agent! . While the show will primarily focus on the Taiwanese entertainment industry, their goal is to appeal to a broader Chinese-language market. It will also be distributed in the United States via Golden TV. Per Steve Chicorel, who is the co-founder and CEO of Organic Media Group, this includes " inviting superstars from Hong Kong, Singapore, Malaysia, Asian-Americans, and yes, even China to join the cast ." The project, which is still looking for funding, has producer Natacha Devillers ( Hector and the Search for Happiness , Asterix & Obelix: The Middle Kingdom ) attached, alongside writer Yang Jingxiang and director Wu Zhongtian ( A Murderous Affair in Horizon Tower ). This announcement marks at least the 14th time that an international remake of the beloved comedy series has been circled by producers. In addition to a Latin America-set adaptation that was announced to be in the works with producer Eva Longoria in 2023, the Filipino adaptation Call My Manager has also been announced , as have versions from the Middle East and Malaysia. As of October 27, Eva Longoria is also in talks to appear in the Call My Agent! movie. Call My Agent! has already been adapted in many other territories , including Britain (as Ten Percent \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b), South Korea ( Behind Every Star ), Türkiye ( Menajerimi Ara ), \u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200b\u200bIndia ( Call My Agent: Bollywood ), Italy ( Call My Agent - Italia ), Germany ( Call My Agent Berlin ), Indonesia ( Hubungi Agen Gue! ), Poland ( Mój agent ), and the Czech Republic and Slovakia ( Vytoč mého agenta ). Ultimately, it makes sense why this new version of the series would be targeting Chinese markets across the globe rather than singling out the Taiwanese market. The Chinese-language market has become increasingly mighty in the entertainment space. This year has seen the market come even more to the fore with the success of 2025\'s Ne Zha 2 , a Mandarin-language animated movie that is currently the highest-grossing movie of the year. In addition to grossing $2.2 billion worldwide, its stellar performance marks the first time that any movie in history has grossed more than $1 billion in a single territory (in this case, China). While it remains to be seen if this new version of Call My Agent! makes it to the air, the franchise\'s malleable format continues to prove itself to be a huge asset. By taking a character-driven approach peppered with flashy celebrity cameos, the show has gained a robust global fanbase in the 10 years since it originally premiered. By: Entertainment Desk Mumbai | Updated: November 12, 2025 06:13 PM IST 3 min read Whatsapp twitter Facebook Reddit PRINT Pope Leo XIV Naturally, whatever Pope Leo XIV, the head of the Roman Catholic Church, says becomes a global talking point . Now, even more so, as he has revealed his all-time favorite films in a recent conversation with Variety. The Pope’s selection reflects an appreciation for works that have become both cultural landmarks and cinematic touchstones, films that, to borrow the words of Martin Scorsese, embody what “absolute cinema” can be. The first film mentioned by him is widely regarded as one of the best Christmas movies ever made, Frank Capra’s 1946 classic It’s a Wonderful Life. No wonder, in 1998, the American Film Institute named It’s a Wonderful Life the 11th greatest American movie of all time. Next on Pope Leo XIV’s list was a universally beloved musical, The Sound of Music (1965), starring Julie Andrews. It is hardly surprising that the film went on to win five Academy Awards, as it so thoroughly deserved to. The Pope also cited Ordinary People (1980), a family drama that explores grief and healing within a wealthy American household. The film is often hailed as a gold standard for cinematic portrayals of mental health and emotional vulnerability. Finally, the Pontiff named the Italian masterpiece La Vita è Bella (Life Is Beautiful), a moving World War II film that balances tragedy and humor in its portrayal of a father’s love for his son. After all, tragedy and comedy are often two faces of the same truth. Having written over 300 articles in just over a year, Billy regularly covers the biggest TV shows and films releasing while also analysing some of the most underrated properties that may slip your attention. Having studied for an MA in Screenwriting at UAL in 2023, Billy honed his writing skills and also developed his ability to critique the work of other creative minds. Before that, Billy studied politics at the University of Nottingham, which helped him to bring nuanced and scholarly analysis to the frameworks within which filmmakers and writers have framed their thematic messages. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap A24 is rightfully respected as one of the most artistic studios in Hollywood, going through a meteoric rise with films like Moonlight , Hereditary , and Everything, Everywhere, All at Once , putting it at the center of discussion in different genres and always around awards season. However, one of their best films has tragically gone under the radar: 20th Century Women . This coming-of-age drama features a stacked cast that examines how people find their purpose and true nature, and whether those are determined by the self or by society. The film was nominated for Best Original Screenplay at the Academy Awards, but that doesn\'t give nearly enough credit to the trio of actresses who carry the narrative and make it so engaging. Despite being set in 1979, the film\'s themes feel incredibly relevant to this day and, despite being incredibly indie, never feels overdone or like it is taking itself too seriously. It will make you laugh and cry, but as 20th Century Women argues, that is far better than feeling nothing at all. \'20th Century Women\' Explores a Mother and Son\'s Strained Relationship Annette Bening smoking a cigarette in 20th Century Women. Image via A24 Mike Mills \' exceptional drama centers on the relationship between Dorothea ( Annette Bening ) and her son, Jamie ( Lucas Jade Zumann ). Since he went through adolescence, Dorothea finds it increasingly difficult to connect with her 15-year-old son, as he seems not only not to know himself, but also to be a part of a generation increasingly more divisive compared to their predecessors, which fits with the counter-culture setting of the late 1970s. In an effort to reconnect and help her son discover who he wants to be, Dorothea enlists the help of her tenant, the punk-rock Abbie ( Greta Gerwig ), and Jamie\'s best friend, the depressed and opinionated Julie ( Elle Fanning ). However, that doesn\'t mean Dorothea doesn\'t have her own issues to contend with, as her generation is too closed off to truly speak their mind, which serves as the true source of conflict in her relationship with her son. There are tonnes of comedy and wild moments featuring funny sexual encounters and blunt lines of dialogue, but the tragic undertone running throughout 20th Century Women means the comedy feels like only a brief distraction from the engaging issues these characters are going through. Greta Gerwig, Annette Bening, and Elle Fanning Shine in \'20th Century Women\' As the title of the film and this article suggest, the stars of 20th Century Women are undoubtedly Bening’s Dorothea, Fanning’s Julie, and Gerwig’s Abbie, especially when they are in scenes together, because all three are so different. Each of them has a different idea of how to help Jamie become a man. Abbie believes he must learn about women to understand how to be a good man towards them, introducing him to feminist theory , whereas Julie has a more toxic idea of masculinity that she has developed through her experiences with boys of her age, believing what she sees must be the correct way of being. Dorothea arguably gives Jamie the most free rein to be who he wants to be, but more because of her own lack of self-analysis that she refuses to examine. Related The 25 Best Movies About Mother-Son Relationships, Ranked Alexa, play the \'Hereditary\' monologue. Posts 2 By Daniela Gama Aug 13, 2025 In hindsight, Bening feels dreadfully snubbed with her lack of accolades for this performance. Her performance portrays her as both caring and emotionally stunted. When Jamie abandons her at one point to go to the city with some friends, she is clearly worried about him, telling him to let her know next time, yet she won\'t show that to anybody. She instead uses the excuse that she merely wants to know if she shouldn\'t cook as much dinner next time, a heartbreaking deflection that balances both her lack of honesty and her desire to provide for her son. \'20th Century Women\' Feels Remarkably Relevant to Today Throughout 20th Century Women , it is impossible to forget that it is set in 1979, with the wardrobe, constant smoking, and politics all reminding the viewer they are in the past. However, that doesn\'t stop it from feeling extremely pertinent to the challenges facing many people today. The idea of how men should interact with, not shy away from, feminism is a topic still fiercely debated online, yet no better moment encapsulates the contemporary relevance of 20th Century Women than when it shows Jimmy Carter\'s "Crisis of Confidence" speech. In this speech, the former President remarks on how everyone feels like they are lacking a purpose, that we all feel there is meant to be more to life than the current format. Indeed, with the rise of identity politics, people\'s individual sense of purpose has never been more unknown, yet Carter\'s argument, and seemingly Mike Mills\', is that the purpose is not that of the individual, but of society. In the same way that Jamie needs a range of different people to raise him, society needs a range of lived experiences living together cohesively to survive. Few will come away from 20th Century Women without learning something about themselves or those around them. Perhaps that is what makes it so underrated. That’s where Catherine Bloom comes in. In her capacity as the longtime go-to personal shopper at Neiman Marcus, she became the style whisperer to the industry elite, her influence visible at most major red carpets. “Catherine Bloom is a staple name in Hollywood,” says stylist Linda Medvene, whose clients include Denzel Washington, Annette Bening and Geena Davis. “She always has pieces you can’t find anywhere else.” Related Stories News Welcome to Hollywood! Coffee Shop Says About You Given Bloom’s decades-long tenure at Neiman Marcus, it caused a stir in L.A. fashion circles this year when she took her talents to rival Nordstrom, which hired her as its first director of luxury styling. In late October, she opened her own store under the retailer’s auspices: Catherine Bloom for Nordstrom. “We want to invite you into our home,” Bloom tells THR about the expansive new studio. “It’s very warm, beautiful and chic, with a more interesting assortment than you’re traditionally used to seeing in most stores.” Interior designer Brigette Romanek, whose clients include Beyoncé and Gwyneth Paltrow, was hired to overhaul the space. “What made this project truly special was the synergy with Catherine,” says Romanek. “This wasn’t just about designing a space — it was about creating a mood, a moment, an experience.” Perched on the corner of Melrose Place and Orlando Avenue, complete with valet and a discreet side entrance, the by-appointment-only studio is drenched in neutrals: cream floors, a plush chocolate brown sofa, suede wall coverings and an array of vintage seating vignettes. And lining the walls are the stars of the show — meticulously curated racks of color-coordinated confections courtesy of such designers as Georges Hobeika, Gabriela Hearst and Valentino, along with McQueen and vintage John Galliano for Dior. Bloom’s industry clientele would expect nothing less. “Catherine is the ultimate curator,” says Blair Rich, CMO and CCO of Legendary Entertainment. “It’s more than just searching the Paris collections for the perfect dress and matching it with a shoe you never thought of but makes the look. She understands lifestyle; what you need not just to look your best but also feel your best, from the office to a black-tie event to a casual weekend away.” This story appeared in the Nov. 5 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. Tim Burton had a hell of a run in the ‘80s and early ‘90s. He fired off hit after hit...until Mars Attacks! . The movie with an all-star cast and some really funny aliens bombed at the box office, but it didn’t deserve to. In fact, I would say it’s one of Burton’s best movies . It had a reported budget of around $80 million, not including marketing, and it made about $100 million in theaters. That's not the worst performance, but it almost certainly lost a lot of money, something a Burton film rarely does. (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) At The Time, It Was Crushed By Critics In his 1996 review of the movie, Roger Ebert wrote : “ Mars Attacks! plays like one of those ’50s movies that are *not* remembered as cult classics.” Rita Kempley at the Washington Post said it was “aimlessly plotted and blandly written.” Review after review panned the tribute to ‘50s sci-fi movies. That was reflected, obviously, in the middling-to-poor box office receipts. Over the years, however, critics have come around. Burton, unsurprisingly, was ahead of his time. If the critics weren’t ready for it then, more modern critiques have been much kinder to the film, and it’s deserving of that. Very deserving. Mars Attacks! Is A Great Movie If you take yourself back to 1996, Burton was at the height of his powers in Hollywood. Starting with his first movie , Pee-Wee’s Big Adventure in 1985, he made one great film after another. A list including Beetlejuice , Batman, and Edward Scissorhands , the latter of which kicked off a long working relationship with Johnny Depp . It really seemed like the quirky director with a look and style all his own couldn’t be stopped. Then, in 1994, he hit his first bump in the road with Ed Wood . That film, a biopic of the legendary B-movie director, was a small-budget movie that generated modest box office receipts. Mars Attacks! followed in 1996 and was his first legitimate bomb. It shouldn’t be remembered for that (and isn’t). Burton enlisted a truly talented roster of actors for the movie that included up-and-comers like Natalie Portman and Lukas Haas. This was alongside some of Hollywood’s most established talent, like Michael J. Fox , Glenn Close, Danny DeVito , Sarah Jessica Parker , Annette Bening, Martin Short , and James Bond himself, Pierce Brosnan . It also crucially features Jack Nicholson in one of his most underrated performances in not one, but two roles. Mars Attacks! is also really funny and just plain fun. It’s completely absurd in all the best ways, and in ways that only a mind like Burton’s could imagine. I’m glad it is well thought of today, because otherwise, it would be another lost classic. Meanwhile, Tim Burton has been busy lately , with last year’s Beetlejuice Beetlejuice and Wednesday , both of which you can watch with a Netflix subscription . (Photo by Jordan Strauss/Invision/AP) State officials will be unveiling a Florida Historical Marker in Fort Lauderdale on Thursday to commemorate Diana Nyad\'s incredible 110-mile swim from Cuba to Key West without a shark cage. Succeeding on her fifth attempt at age 64, Nyad became the first person to swim from Cuba to the Keys without a shark cage — despite battling stinging jellyfish, nausea and other physical and mental challenges. She completed the historic feat in 2013. Nyad\'s swim was later turned into a feature film , "Nyad," starring Annette Bening as the swimmer and Jodie Foster as Stoll, her friend and trainer. The recognition is particularly significant as Nyad is also the first openly LGBTQ+ person in Florida to receive a state historical marker. The dedication ceremony will be held at the Las Olas Oceanside Park in Fort Lauderdale. It is set to begin Thursday at 10 a.m. and is open to the public. Admission is free. The event is scheduled to feature remarks from local and state leaders, as well as members of the LGBTQ+ and women\'s communities and friends of Nyad. Speaking to Rolling Stone for the 30th anniversary of the film’s release, he said, “Look, [ The American President ] is a romantic comedy, but the two political issues at the heart of it were guns and the environment, right? The movie wouldn’t get made today — a studio wouldn’t agree to make it — because they would know you’ve just alienated half the potential audience, which wasn’t the case in 1995. The heroes I wrote in those two stories, they did things even though it would cost them popularity, which is not something you see professional politicians of either party do very often.” The feature, directed by Rob Reiner, follows popular Democratic president Andrew Shepherd (Michael Douglas) seeking reelection. But when the widowed incumbent falls for an environmental lobbyist (Annette Bening), a Republican challenger (Richard Dreyfuss) spots an opportunity to launch an attack campaign. Meanwhile, as Shepherd’s approval rating slips, he seeks to secure the passage of a crucial gun control bill. When asked if The West Wing creator sees any parallels between Republican officials and Dreyfuss’ Bob Rumson, he said, “All I see in the Republican Party today is a creepy, weird fealty to someone who doesn’t deserve it.” He continued later in the interview, “During Covid, I binged every Netflix documentary about cults — NXIVM and the Way Down Cult and Sarah Lawrence, everything. And what they all have in common is this weird, passionate devotion to an utterly unremarkable person. That’s where I feel we are now. I see the man-on-the-street interviews where people are calling Donald Trump authentic and honest, and he means what he says, [I think] you got to be kidding me. What’s new is this strange, cult-like devotion to the very last person who would deserve it. The electorate changed, and I’m not good at explaining what changed it. Maybe the left drove people out of their minds.” Sorkin has previously spoken about how his projects centering on civic duty would translate to modern audiences in our current political landscape. Last year, he voiced similar sentiments , saying of the right-wing party portrayed in The West Wing : “Right now, it would be implausible that the opposition party, that the Republican Party, was reasonable. People would watch that and it would be unfamiliar to them as the country they live in. On the show, while the Republicans were the opposition, they were reasonable.” The filmmaker/writer is currently working on the anticipated followup to 2010’s The Social Network , for which he penned the script. Titled The Social Reckoning , the drama is slated for release Oct. 9, 2026. Despite receiving a great deal of undue criticism from a vocal minority, Captain Marvel is one of the most important, powerful, and game-changing characters existing in the MCU right now. It would be a huge shame if she wasn’t involved with Avengers: Doomsday , especially since she not only has an intimate knowledge of the MCU’s cosmos — which will play a role in the Russo brothers’ upcoming sequel — but also because she is now residing on Earth. Danvers could easily be recruited into Sam Wilson’s new Avengers team , perhaps even becoming a leader among them. Rambeau was met by X-Men members Beast (Kelsey Grammer) and Binary (Lashana Lynch), perfectly setting up the appearance of the X-Men in Avengers: Doomsday , but only if Rambeau returns — and her Aunt Carol shouldn’t be far behind. Captain Marvel’s almost-unmatched level of power, given to her after she absorbed the energy of the Space Stone from Mar-Vell’s (Annette Bening) light-speed engine, means Danvers may be powerful enough to go toe-to-toe with Doctor Doom. Doom is expected to scour the multiverse in Avengers: Doomsday in hopes of stopping incursions by destroying other worlds and variants, but he’ll come under opposition by many of the MCU’s heroes. Danvers held her own against Thanos (Josh Brolin) in Endgame , so would also be an invaluable asset in the fight against Doom in Doomsday , so we really hope she returns. What do you think? Speaking with Entertainment Tonight at the recent CMA Awards, Kebbell gave an update on the filming progress of Y: Marshals and noted that she’s relieved and grateful that a release date is finally set. The Vampire Diaries and 9-1-1 alum adds that the team has worked extremely hard, with filming ending in about three weeks . Read her quote below: We\'ve been working so hard. Executive produced by franchise creator Taylor Sheridan , Y: Marshals will see Kayce leave the Yellowstone Ranch to join an elite U.S. Marshals unit, using his experience as a cowboy and his complicated past to deliver justice across Montana. In the process, he\'ll have to navigate family, responsibility, and the job’s heavy psychological toll. Grimes is joined in the series by several returning and new actors, with Kebbell playing a fellow U.S. Marshal. In an interview with Rolling Stone, he reflected on the film’s themes, noting that studios today might hesitate due to its political messaging. Aaron Sorkin on The American President’s Modern Relevance Sorkin argued that the film’s dual focus on guns and environmental issues could alienate potential viewers. He pointed out, “A studio wouldn’t agree to make it because they would know you’ve just alienated half the potential audience.” This sentiment highlights the changing landscape of political discourse and audience reception since the film’s release. Overview of The American President Director: Rob Reiner Release Year: 1995 Stars: Michael Douglas as President Andrew Shepherd, Annette Bening as an environmental lobbyist, Richard Dreyfuss as Republican challenger Bob Rumson The plot centers on President Shepherd as he navigates reelection while facing both political and personal challenges. As his approval ratings drop, he tries to push through a significant gun control bill amid a budding romance with a lobbyist. Sorkin’s Views on Today’s Politics Sorkin also drew parallels between contemporary political figures and Rumson’s character, expressing concern over a “cult-like devotion” to unremarkable leaders. He linked this phenomenon to a broader shift in the electorate, stating, “The electorate changed, and I’m not good at explaining what changed it.” Reflecting on his previous work, Sorkin mentioned that the portrayal of the Republican Party in The West Wing would seem unrealistic to modern viewers. He stated, “Right now, it would be implausible that the opposition party was reasonable.” Such comments underscore the evolving perception of political dynamics among audiences. Upcoming Projects Currently, Sorkin is working on his new project, The Social Reckoning, which serves as a sequel to his acclaimed film, The Social Network. It is expected to premiere on October 9, 2026. As Sorkin continues to explore themes of civic duty and political engagement, the challenges of adapting to today’s audience remain evident. Recommended Stories “Die Another Day. 0070 James Bond Party for the one and only @krisjenner 70th birthday!!!" Kim captioned the carousel, referencing the theme of the night. Kim’s outfit featured a sheer lilac mesh crop top adorned with sparkling crystals and delicate straps that crisscrossed along her back, paired with a coordinating low-waisted column skirt that shimmered under the lights. The body-hugging silhouette was so snug that a video showed Kim carefully taking small steps on her way to the party. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kim Kardashian (@kimkardashian) The SKIMS founder completed her look with a sleek updo accented by soft curls, luminous purple-toned makeup, and matching accessories, striking the perfect balance between elegance and glamour. One of the photos in her post showed Halle Berry in her original Bond look beside Pierce Brosnan, drawing a direct line between inspiration and homage. A Star-Packed 007 Celebration Kris Jenner’s milestone bash was as lavish as one might expect hosted at Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sánchez’s Beverly Hills mansion, and attended by a constellation of Hollywood’s biggest names. Among the high-profile guests were Oprah Winfrey, Mariah Carey, Tyler Perry, Vin Diesel, and Mark Zuckerberg. It was also a night out for celebrity couples, with Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, as well as Adele and Rich Paul, among the glamorous attendees. The Kardashian-Jenner Clan Brings the Glam Naturally, Kris’s daughters turned the event into a runway of their own. Kourtney Kardashian, Kendall Jenner, and Kylie Jenner joined Kim in celebrating their momager’s milestone alongside Travis Barker, Scott Disick, Tristan Thompson, and Kris’s longtime partner Corey Gamble. Kendall, who recently marked her 30th birthday on Nov. 3, stunned in a figure-hugging red fishtail gown paired with sleek black The Row sandals. Kylie opted for a white halter-neck cutout gown by Elisabetta Franchi with a sheer floor-length skirt, white pointed pumps, and glittering Lorraine Schwartz earrings. Image credits: getty images, canva Hollywood star Halle Berry has taken aim at California Governor Gavin Newsom, but not over a film role, an awards snub, or a political endorsement. This time, the dispute is over menopause care — and Berry is treating it with the seriousness of a long-ignored public health crisis. The veto that triggered the backlash The flashpoint came last month when Newsom vetoed the Menopause Care Equity Act, a bill that had enjoyed rare bipartisan approval in Sacramento. The proposed law would have required insurance plans to cover evidence-based menopause treatments and mandated proper medical training for physicians. Supporters called it a practical step toward fixing a long-standing gap in women’s healthcare. Newsom blocked it, citing cost concerns Berry’s response was swift. In a widely discussed op-ed with Illinois Lt Governor Juliana Stratton and menopause researcher Dr Pauline Maki, she criticised the veto as a setback for millions of women. She argued that California, a state that often defines itself as a national trendsetter, had fallen behind on a fundamental issue of women’s health. A larger failure of the healthcare system Berry’s frustration is rooted in the broader reality: for decades, menopause has been poorly understood, under-researched and widely dismissed. Millions of women experience symptoms each year, yet most doctors receive little to no training in diagnosing or treating them. As a result, many women spend years navigating misdiagnoses, stigma and avoidable suffering. Berry herself has spoken about being misdiagnosed during perimenopause, underscoring what she calls a systemic blind spot in American medicine. Other states are stepping up While California pulled back, several other states have accelerated reforms. Illinois has rolled out a series of measures — from mandatory insurance coverage for FDA-approved menopause treatments beginning in 2026 to launching its first Menopause Awareness Week. Michigan, Pennsylvania, New York, Wisconsin, Maine and Rhode Island have also introduced bills or initiatives addressing menopause education, workplace protections and treatment coverage. What was once a neglected subject is now emerging as a genuine policy frontier. Berry’s unexpected leadership role Berry’s advocacy has helped propel that shift. Far from the usual celebrity activism, her effort is grounded in personal experience and a clear call for structural change: better medical curriculum, wider insurance coverage and workplaces that recognise menopause as a legitimate health transition, not an inconvenience. Her central argument is straightforward — menopause is not a disease, but women deserve competent care. And policymakers who claim to support gender equity cannot ignore the needs of women in midlife, a demographic that drives a significant share of the country’s workforce and leadership. The bottom line Newsom’s veto has triggered a rare political dynamic: California, long seen as a pioneer in progressive health policy, is being outpaced by states across the Midwest and Northeast. And Halle Berry, one of Hollywood’s most recognisable figures, has unexpectedly emerged as a national voice for menopause reform. Whether the governor reconsiders his stance remains to be seen. But Berry’s message is already reverberating: menopause is no longer a footnote in women’s health — and ignoring it now comes with political consequences. Alongside interviewing stars such as Selin Hizli , Rose Ayling-Ellis , and Chelsea Peretti , Jake was lucky enough to visit the set of Aardman and Netflix\'s Wallace and Gromit: A Vengeance Most Fowl in 2024, getting the chance to chat with four-time Academy Award winner Nick Park and Merlin Crossingham . However, in 2024, her new horror movie Never Let Go simply couldn\'t handle the level of genre competition it was facing, sadly falling into box office obscurity. Perhaps if released this year, given the sheer absence of many new horror films during Halloween weekend, the Lionsgate release would\'ve fared better. However, with competition including the likes of the Naomi Scott -led Smile 2 and the Academy-recognized body horror hit The Substance , Never Let Go really never stood a chance. However, a year on, and the lack of new horror options is causing Never Let Go to find popularity on streaming, even if spooky season is now in the rearview mirror. At the time of writing, Never Let Go has quietly joined the top ten most-streamed movies on Starz in the U.S. The horror flick has taken tenth position in a list packed with eye-catching titles, from the Nicolas Cage -led Arsenal to the recent Ana de Armas -led John Wick spin-off, From the World of John Wick: Ballerina . Receiving a lukewarm critical reception upon arrival, the film only managed middling scores of 56% and 54% from critics and audiences on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, with the site\'s consensus reading, "Director Alexandre Aja \'s latest horror offering boasts anxiety-inducing atmosphere and a committed performance from Halle Berry, although audiences will have to let go of some storytelling expectations to enjoy the ride." A synopsis of the movie reads: "In this psychological thriller/horror, as an Evil takes over the world beyond their front doorstep, the only protection for a mother and her twin sons is their house and their family\'s protective bond. Needing to stay connected at all times – even tethering themselves with ropes – they cling to one another, urging each other to never let go. But when one of the boys questions if the evil is real, the ties that bind them together are severed, triggering a terrifying fight for survival." Just How Bad Was \'Never Let Go\'s Box Office Run? In the grand scheme of box office flops, Never Let Go wasn\'t a total failure, at least managing to return its reported $20 million budget. With a $21.7 million global haul , split between $10.3 million in domestic revenue and $11.4 million from overseas markets, the film simply couldn\'t keep up with its tough competition, finishing fourth in the domestic rankings on its opening weekend, and quickly slipping to eighth by its second weekend. Interestingly, out of this global total, nearly 50% has come from North America and the remaining half from international markets. While the seventh installment in the Predator franchise has crossed its production budget of $105 million (as per Variety), it’s yet to break even at the box office. Given its current momentum and positive word-of-mouth, Predator: Badlands should outgross Gothika very soon. In fact, by the time you’re reading this, it may have already surpassed this target. How Much More Predator: Badlands Needs To Break Even? Made on an estimated production budget of $105 million, the latest Predator entry needs to earn around $262.5 million worldwide to break even at the box office, using the 2.5x multiplier rule. With its current global haul of $140.2 million, Badlands needs to bring in another $122.3 million globally to reach its break-even point before it begins to generate profits. More About Predator: Badlands The film follows Dek (Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi), a young Predator outcast from his clan, who forms an unexpected alliance with Thia ( Elle Fanning ), a damaged synthetic owned by the Weyland-Yutani Corporation. Together, the duo undertakes a dangerous journey across the wastelands in search of the ultimate enemy. (Photo by Matt Licari/Invision/AP) NEW YORK – The greatest mystery in Rian Johnson’s “Knives Out” movies might be Benoit Blanc. Over the course of three films, Johnson and Daniel Craig have stingily dropped clues to Blanc’s past and personal life. Since Blanc first introduced himself in “Knives Out” as “a respectful, quiet, passive observer … of the truth,” following the breadcrumbs has been a sport of its own. Recommended Videos There are, for instance, the vague, offhand references to cases he’s cracked before: something with a tennis champion, another with a ballet dancer and, in the latest chapter, “Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery,” we hear about something dastardly at the Kentucky Derby that he solved. Blanc has been profiled in The New Yorker and a guest on “The View.” He appears to live with Hugh Grant. He dislikes the board game Clue. Having been caught singing Sondheim and, in the new one, humming “Skimbleshanks: The Railway Cat,” from “Cats,” we know he loves musical theater. Over the course of the “Knives Out” trilogy, Johnson and Craig have colored in Blanc with sporadic and comic revelations, adding subtle, and sometimes personal, characteristics. “I’m not as much into musical theater as Rian,” Craig says, sitting beside his director in a recent interview. “So he claims in front of a microphone,” adds Johnson. Every “Knives Out” movie is wholesale change. New setting. New case. New cast of characters. But Craig and Johnson are the mainstays. Together, they’ve turned Blanc, the last of the gentleman sleuths, into one of the greatest — “Halle Berry!” — protagonists in recent movies. In “Wake Up Dead Man,” which opens in theaters Wednesday and hits Netflix on Dec. 12, Blanc takes up the case of a monsignor (Josh Brolin) who dies mysteriously in the middle of a church service. Of the movie’s many delights — among them, Josh O’Connor’s co-leading performance as a priest under suspicion and a cast of parishioners including Andrew Scott, Jeremy Renner and Glenn Close — is seeing Craig continue to find new little wrinkles to Blanc. ‘A Southern lilt’ Rather than being set in stone, Blanc has evolved. Take that accent. The first script, Johnson recalls, described “the slightest hint of a Southern lilt.” But Craig, taking inspiration from Tennessee Williams and Shelby Foote, pushed the accent closer to, as Chris Evans\' character says in “Knives Out”: a “Kentucky-fried Foghorn Leghorn drawl.” In “Glass Onion,” he laid it on even thicker, part of a scheme revealed only later into the film. “My biggest fear was that it would devolve,” Craig says, chuckling. “If it ever becomes pastiche, it’s like, ‘Whoa, let’s get out of here.’ God knows I’m not comparing myself to Gene Wilder, but the way Gene Wilder did comedy was: It’s all through truth. As long as you’re as truthful as you can get in that situation, the funny comes out.” As thoroughly established in the role as Craig is, he very nearly missed out on Benoit Blanc. Craig was initially unavailable for “Knives Out” due to production on “No Time to Die.” Johnson sought other possible actors. “It was literally five weeks later we were shooting. We didn’t think you were available,” Johnson says. “Then something happened where suddenly you guys got delayed for three months and we had a window.” “I read it and I was shocked that someone would send this to me,” Craig says. “Overjoyed. I saw it from the off-go. I read it and I visualized it. It’s a testament to his writing. I mean, come on. Benoit Blanc.” \'Halle Berry!\' In forming the role, Craig took inspiration from Jacques Tati’s debonair but bumbling Monsieur Hulot and Cary Grant’s elegant panache in “To Catch a Thief.” He combed through out-of-print books of Southern expressions. (One that got cut: “Butter my buns and call me a biscuit.”) Along the way, Craig has improvised some of Blanc’s best expressions. In “Wake Up Dead Man,” he suddenly blurts out, as if moved by the swelling whodunit hijinks: “Scooby Dooby Doo!” A sip of Jeremy Renner-sponsored hot sauce in “Glass Onion” led to the infamous “Halle Berry!” “All of the best lines in there are things Daniel just brings,” says Johnson. “He says, ‘What about this?’ and I start laughing. And it’s the best line in the movie.” “I have a security team and there’s a guy that says it,” Craig says of the etymology of “Halle Berry.” “I stole it. I said, ‘Can I have that?’ and he said ‘Yep.’” For Craig and Johnson, Blanc has been an ongoing conversation. “Wake Up Dead Man,” the most sincere of the three mysteries, deals significantly with matters of faith and religion. The two worked to sharpen Blanc\'s perspective. In the film, he declares himself “a proud heretic. I kneel at the altar of the rational.” Then there are the ornate flourishes of dialogue Johnson pens for Blanc. Modeled on Agatha Christie’s Hercule Poirot, Blanc is the knowing product of a rich literary tradition, dusted off for modern times. In contemporary satires, Blanc is the retro lynchpin. That means Craig delivering lines like “I suspect foul play” silhouetted against a fireplace, and vowing to uncover “what this flock of wicked wolves is hiding” while framed in a stained-glass window. “Delicious,” Craig says with a grin. A franchise of their own It’s ironic that, on the heels of their own experiences with iconic film series, Johnson and Craig have built a franchise all their own. Johnson released “Knives Out” two years after the much-debated “Star Wars: The Last Jedi.” As he exited the James Bond films, Craig donned the suit of another justice-seeker, albeit one with much different swimwear . “I don’t think either of us really thought about it that way,” Johnson says. “It’s just been making one movie after another, just trying to keep it challenging and fresh for ourselves. It feels almost accidental that suddenly we’ve made three. It definitely wasn’t setting out to build, God forbid, the filthiest word in the universe, IP. We’re just trying to make movies.” “I’ve been doing this for long enough that as soon as you start counting your chickens on a job, it’s all over,” adds Craig. Yet it’s now possible, especially as the two contemplate a fourth “Knives Out” film, that there are young moviegoers who know Craig more as Benoit Blanc than they do that other B-name. If Johnson and Craig do keep “Knives Out” going, even as a two-film deal with Netflix concludes, it will allow Johnson the chance to restock his whodunit cupboard. But it will just as surely offer the opportunity to relaunch, and play with, Blanc. “I really love, in my mystery detectives, for them to be kind of enigmas. It pointedly doesn’t work when you start digging into backstory with the detective,” says Johnson. “That’s always kind of boring because character is only revealed through action and the action of a detective is such a strong thing. He’s there to solve the case.” In some ways, Blanc is like a movie star. He shows up, dazzles and goes home to his largely unseen private life. Craig likes it that way. “Going back to ‘Death on the Nile’ and ‘Evil Under the Sun,’ Petey (Ustinov) turns up looking glorious from somewhere — who knows where, some party in the South of France,” says Craig. “And he ends up leaving in the end and going off somewhere. He’s sort of alienated from the rest of the people. He has to be because he’s the guy who suspects everybody.” Every few years, Benoit Blanc comes and goes. Everything in between is a riddle.
